//: The MEETING NOTIFIER's other half. The lab POSTs one JSON body here when a minutes run has written its outputs back into the tenant; this flow turns that into a message in the MEETING'S OWN CHAT. It exists because Microsoft Graph refuses to create a chat message with application permissions (that path is migration-only) and the lab authenticates as an application by design — so the only thing that can post as a person is something already holding a person's Teams connection, which is exactly what a Power Automate connection is. Two actions and no polling: the lab pushes when there is something to say, and stays silent otherwise.

When_a_Teams_webhook_request_is_received.//: The SAME trigger the approval channel uses (TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL) — a Workflows webhook, not an O365 connector, which Microsoft disabled between 18 and 22 May 2026. Copy the URL it generates after saving into `.env` as MEETING_WEBHOOK_URL and redeploy the notifier. The schema below is what `lab.substrate.meeting_notifier.announcement()` sends; keep the two in step, because a field missing from the schema is silently absent in the designer rather than an error.

Append_a_link.//:
ONLY the tags this field actually honours. Measured on two live messages: `` rendered as a clean clickable filename, while `

` and `

    ` appeared as literal text — the field SANITISES rather than escapes. A plain-text version then lost the links entirely AND collapsed its newlines, because the field is HTML underneath and whitespace does not survive it. So: anchors for links, `
    ` for breaks, no block tags.

Compose_the_message.//:
The Message field ESCAPES text typed into it at design time but does NOT escape a token's RUNTIME value — measured on two live messages: a typed

arrived as literal text while an carried in by variables('Links') rendered as a real link. So the whole body is built HERE and the Message field holds nothing but this action's output. The action's own code view cannot be used instead: it reports "'Message' is required" and never commits.
Compose_the_message.inputs:
@concat('The minutes for this meeting are ready.
', triggerBody()?['speakers'], ' speaker(s), ', triggerBody()?['decisions'], ' decision(s), ', triggerBody()?['actions'], ' action(s)

', variables('Links'), '
They are saved beside the recording; opening them still needs your usual access to that folder.')

Post_in_the_meeting_chat.//: STEP 2. 'Post message in a chat or channel' (operationId PostMessageToConversation), location 'Group chat', recipient taken from the body. No meeting TITLE in the message: the lab never has it (a minutes run is a continuation started from a transcript reference, not from a meeting) and this posts into the meeting's own conversation, where the title is already on screen — that is the whole point: the destination is the meeting's own conversation, resolved by the lab from the recording, never a chat picked here. `chat_id` is the meeting's threadId as Graph reports it (19:meeting_...@thread.v2). Poster 'User' posts as the OWNER of this flow's Teams connection, who must be a member of that chat; 'Flow bot' is the alternative and needs the bot to be able to reach the chat. See README for which to choose.
